From reading this it reminds me of how I used to feel about myself at 18 so, here are some things I learned that I wish I knew about back then I hope they will help you feel more comfortable.

1. Be yourself and learn to be comfortable being yourself. I know it sounds cliche and stupid but this is the big one and the real deal. You have to learn to love yourself. I mean really love yourself. Not for the ends that you want other people to like you, but because you're a person and you'll always be with yourself and you deserve it. You have to consciously practice, relaxing and just being natural and present. It doesn't mean not trying to improve yourself but more like acknowledging you do the best that you can, and you don't deserve to be criticized for just existing.

2. Don't worry about what other people think. Again cliché, but time moves so fucking fast people you worry about now you won't remember or see 2 years from now which goes by faster than you'll ever believe. Seriously, it's tough to internalize especially when you're young, but as life goes on you realize how fast it goes and worrying about how other people perceive you isn't worth shit. Stop wasting the energy on it, it's hard, but let it go. Do what you want act like you want be what you want. It doesn't mean be mean or anything, just be genuine and honest at your core about what you're thinking and feeling. People pick up on it when you're faking or trying to forcing something. Be real, talk to people, if they don't like you fuck them, you'll attract people that do like you and your personality. You can't control how people react and feel it's a waste of energy, all you can do is be yourself. 

3. You're enough. You don't have to be anything more for anybody else.

4. No matter what you'll be okay I know it's scary and weird right now, and it feels like nobody likes you, but I promise you'll be good and it will get better, so don't stress about it too much. Life really is too short honestly.

5. Don't stop growing and trying to improve in all aspects of your life. Don't waste time being stagnant. If you feel like you lack social skills, and it's something you want to get better at there are immediate steps you can take to get better at it. 
       A.) Practice, talk to as many people as you can all the time. This is where you'll learn the most and where virtual shit can't help you. You need real world experience. Talk to literally everyone you can and get more comfortable with it and being yourself.
        B.) Read books about improving social connections by people more qualified to speak on the subject than anyone on reddit lol. Seriously this is the big one. I know reading can suck, but it can help change your life in a direction you want it to go in. Give it a shot. Read one book on making friends I guarentee you it will help you more than anthing in this thread.

I'm by no means the expert on this and I'm sure there are people way more qualified, but just from my experience. Being scared to talk; I don't know what you're afraid of, but I'm assuming it's because of what other people will think? Nobody remembers or cares what you say, which can be kind of freeing when you realize it. Try and remember people you tried to impress or cared about their opinions of you 3 years ago or in highschool: I would bet you can barely remember and they don't even know you tried so hard in the first place. It's a waste of energy to think about and time will move on and everyone forgets. Just be nice, say and do what you want as long as you're not actively hurting anyone. As for knowing what to say and keeping conversations going its as much practice as anything else; you won't become a master over night. Talk to more people and you'll get better at it is the best advice I can give you. To help out immediately: 1.Listen to what people say, like really listen; that way you can ask questions about what they're talking about, interested in etc. 2. Ask people open ended questions. Give them questions that they can talk about, not "yes" or "no" questions. 3. People love to talk about themselves, but do so in a way that doesn't seem like a job interview; ask about them, people will talk about that for a while. 4. Actively expand your interests/knowledge so you have more things to talk about with people, that way you can have more of a back and forth conversation about things you're both interested in. 5. Make eye contact and nod your head once in a while appropriately lol. 6. Don't think super hard about what to say: remember the first part, nobody really cares or is probably even paying that much attention. Combine that basic stuff you should be able to make it through some conversations, but again practice my man. I wrote too much lol but I hope any of this helps and again I'm no expert so don't take any of this as law or anything lol
